title: "ldap"
description: "optionally enriches the OIDC identity with directory attributes"
eyebrow: "Configuration"

<!-- Generated by genconfdocs from the config structs in server/config. Do not edit. -->

LDAP is enrichment, never a requirement. If directory data is available a user gets more — extra principals, fresher groups, auto-disable coverage. If it is not, everything still works. Login therefore **fails open**: an LDAP error during the callback logs to the LDAP destination and proceeds with the OIDC-only identity. There is deliberately no `required` knob.  See docs/operations/ldap.md.

## `enabled`

`bool`, default `false`

Turns on the login-time lookup and the background sync.

```yaml
ldap:
  enabled: false
```

## `url`

`string`, default `empty`

The directory server to connect to, e.g. ldaps://ldap.example.net.

```yaml
ldap:
  url: ""
```

## `bind_dn`

`string`, default `empty`

The DN to bind as for the search. Together with `bind_password` this is the implicit "simple" bind mechanism; a keytab-based SASL GSSAPI alternative is tracked separately and slots in beside these keys rather than replacing them.

```yaml
ldap:
  bind_dn: ""
```

## `bind_password`

`string`, default `empty`

The password for `bind_dn`.

```yaml
ldap:
  bind_password: ""
```

## `base_dn`

`string`, default `empty`

The search base for the user lookup, and the default base for field searches that do not name their own.

```yaml
ldap:
  base_dn: ""
```

## `user_filter`

`string`, default `empty`

A Go template over the OIDC identity, with the same idiom as key ID templates: {{.Username}}, {{.Email}}, {{.Subject}}, and {{.Extra.&lt;name>}}. Values are RFC 4515 escaped during rendering and the operator cannot opt out, because a preferred_username containing * or ) is otherwise filter injection.

```yaml
ldap:
  user_filter: ""
```

## `fields`

`map`

Maps destinations to the directory sources that populate them, mirroring OAuthFields with attribute names instead of claim names.

The reserved names are other_accounts, service_accounts and groups. Any other key is an extra template field, captured into the same contract as OAuthFields.Extra: reachable as {{.Extra.&lt;name>}}, stored empty when absent, and never a reason for login to fail. There is no separate extra sub-map; LDAP enrichment is extra by definition.

The merge rule is per field: a configured LDAP field (any attribute or searches) wins over the OIDC value, and an unconfigured one leaves the OIDC value untouched. Override rather than union, because union makes it impossible to retire a stale principal from only one source. Groups are the exception — both sources persist side by side.

username, email and subject are rejected here: the subject keys the user row, the username is what lookups are keyed by, and the OIDC email claim is the source of truth for users.email.

## `group_name_attribute`

`string`, default `empty`

Names the attribute to read a group's name from when a group search is used. When groups arrive as DNs (memberOf, the common case), each DN is reduced to its first RDN value — the CN — and a value that does not parse as a DN is kept as-is. The reduced name is what must match the configured group names.

```yaml
ldap:
  group_name_attribute: ""
```

## `limits`

Caps what one directory can push into the database.

## `limits.max_values_per_attribute`

`int`, default `1000`

Caps a single multi-valued attribute.

```yaml
ldap:
  limits:
    max_values_per_attribute: 1000
```

## `limits.max_entries_per_search`

`int`, default `1000`

Caps the matched entries one field search contributes.

```yaml
ldap:
  limits:
    max_entries_per_search: 1000
```

## `limits.max_attributes_bytes`

`int`, default `65536`

Caps the serialized user_ldap.attributes JSON.

```yaml
ldap:
  limits:
    max_attributes_bytes: 65536
```

## `timeout`

`duration`, default `5s`

Bounds each directory operation. The login callback is on a user-facing path, so this is the entire latency cost enrichment can add to a login.

```yaml
ldap:
  timeout: 5s
```

## `start_tls`

`bool`, default `false`

Upgrades a plain ldap:// connection to TLS. Irrelevant for ldaps:// URLs, which are TLS from the start.

```yaml
ldap:
  start_tls: false
```

## `tls_ca`

`string`, default `empty`

A PEM bundle path to verify the directory's certificate against. Empty uses the system roots.

```yaml
ldap:
  tls_ca: ""
```

## `tls_insecure_skip_verify`

`bool`, default `false`

Disables certificate verification. A homelab escape hatch, logged loudly at startup; it makes the connection trivially interceptable and has no place in production.

```yaml
ldap:
  tls_insecure_skip_verify: false
```
